KEY MESSAGE 1 ...High pressure builds offshore of New England 
tonight ahead of an approaching frontal system that will move 
across the area Sunday and Sunday night.

One more night of fair weather tonight as high pressure builds 
offshore of New England tonight ahead of an approaching frontal 
system. After dewpoints drop during the day today, they will creep 
up again tonight into Sunday morning. Afternoon cumulus clouds will 
continue to develop today and a stray shower might occur for 
southern New Jersey or central/southern portions of Delmarva. But 
most areas will be dry.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Rainy conditions Sunday into Sunday night with 
heavy rainfall possible.

A warm front will lift into the region during the day Sunday, but 
likely not make it past central/southern portions of Delmarva and 
southern New Jersey, before a cold front and triple point low 
approach the area late in the overnight. We expect a couple of 
rounds of precipitation as these systems move into the area. The 
first will begin late morning into the afternoon hours as a short 
wave/vorticity impulse approaches from the west. This round will 
likely be mostly showers with no thunder activity as we will be 
north of the warm front and instability will be minimal to non 
existent. Rainfall with this first batch will likely be mostly 0.25-
0.50 inches or less area-wide.

The next batch is expected to move into the area during the evening 
and overnight hours as the second short wave/vorticity impulse moves 
into the area ahead of the approaching cold front and possible 
triple point low. PWATS continue to increase to 2-2.25 inches, so 
there will remain the threat for heavy rainfall as this rainfall 
moves across the area. It looks like the heavy rainfall will be 
fairly progressive, so we are not planning on a Flash Flood Watch at 
this time. However, there will may still be some localized flash 
flooding if any training does occur, especially in urbanized and 
poor drainage areas as 1-2 inches of rain, with locally higher 
amounts, will be possible overnight

There is still not a lot of instability since we'll still be north 
of the warm front, so thunderstorms are not expected to be 
widespread. They still can't be ruled out however, and any severe 
threat looks to be across portions of southern New Jersey and 
central/southern portions of Delmarva which will be closer to the 
warm front. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...A trailing mid level short wave trough and weak cold 
front may result in another round of showers and thunderstorms 
Monday Afternoon and Evening.

The cold front associated with the low that approaches the region on 
Sunday will finally progress through the region and move off shore 
on Monday. Additionally, in the the mid levels, a trailing short 
wave trough will cross overhead. The net result is that isolated to 
scattered showers and thunderstorms will be possible during the day 
on Monday. 

As for hazards, this round appears to have very limited threats for 
both flash flooding and severe hazards. Convection on Monday will be 
much more weakly forced (as compared to Sunday/Sunday Night), and 
bulk shear values are depicted in the 20 to 25 kt range, which is 
rather modest. This limits the severe threat. Model soundings depict 
still relatively high precipitable water values, and warm cloud 
layers above 10K ft, which results in some heavy rain threat. 
However, with limited shear and coverage of convection, the threat 
for any one area to get heavy rain for long enough to result in 
flash flooding.

For those hoping for a significant cool down in the wake of this 
cold front, unfortunately the temperature gradient is very small. As 
such highs on Tuesday will be at or just a degree or two lower than 
Monday. That being said, the front should usher in drier air, so 
regardless it should feel more comfortable on Tuesday. 

KEY MESSAGE 4...A cold front is expected to cross through the region 
Thursday into Friday.

The next main focus is another cold front arriving in the region 
during the Thursday into Friday time period. There are some big 
timing differences between models on when exactly the front will 
arrive and when the mid level trough will cross off shore. As such, 
there is considerable uncertainty with the potential hazards as 
severe and hydro threat will be dependent on the prime time for any 
showers and thunderstorms.

In terms of temperatures, so far this appears to be a stronger cold 
front than the early week cold front. As such, temperatures going 
into the weekend should be around 5 degrees lower as compared to the 
mid week time period.
